## My thinking this year

Well, I've been farming this land for 40 years, so I mostly know what works. 20 mu isn't a lot, but with six people in the house we manage. My two sons help on weekends and my wife works with me most days, so labor isn't the biggest problem — money for inputs is.

Let me think about how to split up the 20 mu this year. I always keep the bulk of it in wheat-maize because that's our food and stable income — about 12 mu for that. Cotton I've scaled back over the years because the price has been poor and picking is hard work at my age, so I'll keep 5 mu. The chili I started doing a few mu about ten years ago when the price got good — I'll put 3 mu in chili this year. That's 20 mu.

**Wheat (12 mu):** I plant early-to-middle October after I clear the maize. I buy the common improved variety from the agro-shop — I used to save seed but the yields weren't as good. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, maybe 40-50 kg per mu of 15-15-15, then topdress urea at jointing in late February or early March, maybe 15 kg per mu. That works out to around 17 kg N per mu total, which is what I've been doing for years. If it's a dry winter I irrigate at overwintering and then again at jointing and heading — usually 3 times total. My well is metered and it's getting expensive, so I don't irrigate more than I need. Last year I got about 450 kg/mu, that's what I'm hoping for again.

**Maize (12 mu):** Right after the wheat comes off in June, I have to move fast — maybe 3-4 days to get the maize in. I use a hybrid seed, the one the seed dealer sells most of — everyone in the village uses similar. I plant with a seeder I rent from a neighbor for a few yuan per mu. Base fertilizer goes in at planting, and I topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (around V10-V12). About 16 kg N/mu total. Maize here doesn't need as much water as wheat — if July and August rain is normal I might not irrigate at all, or just once. Last year I got about 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton (5 mu):** Cotton is more work but the fiber still sells alright. I plant mid-to-late April after the ground warms up. I use less N on cotton than wheat — maybe 12 kg/mu — because too much N makes it grow tall and delays the bolls. I'll spray for bollworm 2-3 times and do a herbicide at the start. I'll irrigate maybe twice during the season. Family does the picking — that's 3-4 rounds from September into October. Hard on the back.

**Chili (3 mu):** Chili is the money crop but it's risky — price swings a lot. I start seedlings in my little greenhouse in March and transplant in early May. I put down farmyard manure from a neighbor who keeps chickens, plus compound fertilizer. Chili takes more nutrients than grain. I irrigate through the well every 10-15 days in summer because chili dies fast if the soil dries. Need to spray for aphids and anthracnose. Good years I get 2000+ kg/mu fresh, but the price can be 2 yuan or 6 yuan per kg — you never know.

Overall I'm sticking close to what worked last year. Fertilizer prices went up again but I'm not cutting back much because shorting the crop is worse than spending a bit extra. My oldest son wants me to try the new drip system for chili but that's too expensive for me right now — maybe next year if the chili price is good.
